Research Workflow Portal — Wave 7

Source: SITE_RESEARCH_PORTAL.md

Open the browser-local Research Workflow Portal

This website-only navigation layer complements the immutable native R 0.4.3 release. It does not modify or run package estimators in the browser. It combines a local CSV structure inspector, a conservative scientific method-selection wizard and a ten-workflow mapping to actual exported R functions and plots.

Local gaze CSV structural preflight

Data are processed entirely in the browser; no upload, network request, cloud persistence or statistical fitting. It accepts a long-format CSV with participant_id, trial_id, x, y and exactly one time header: time, time_s or time_ms. A strict quoted-CSV parser fails on malformed columns, ambiguous headers, more than 12,000 observations or more than 1.2 million characters. Unit declarations are user-supplied; no rescaling is performed.

The inspection reports aggregate row/participant/trial counts, repeated trial structure, absent and nonnumeric coordinates, missing/duplicate/out-of-order timestamps and common observed-grid structural compatibility only. Exported summary JSON contains no participant/trial identifiers, raw coordinates, raw timestamps or file names. Clear local data erases the tab’s inputs and retained summary.

A separate explicit button can propagate an observed common-grid structure and repeated-participant indicator into the method selector. Failed common-grid compatibility does not automatically classify the observations as sparse or asynchronously acquired.

Method-selection wizard

The selector requires declared observed support, objective, sampling hierarchy and uncertainty ambition. Unsupported combinations produce no automatic selection; it does not silently interpolate, pool repeated trials or assign a model. Requesting identification of missing-not-at-random gaze from observed data alone produces a refusal. Nominal whole-function confidence intervals remain scientifically restricted even where a useful descriptive method exists. This is a navigation tool, not statistical model selection, calibrated inference or a clinical/causal decision.

Exact ten-route native R mapping

All ten Python entries below come from the supported Python 1.2.0 W1–W4 module-scoped workflow layer. All ten matching R orchestration exports and their R estimator references are verified against the immutable R 0.4.3 NAMESPACE. Exported names do not demonstrate identical estimators or complete Python source contracts.

Every interactive row provides source methods, documentation links, a relevant actually rendered native-R example, its reproduction script, method assumptions and scientific limits. Source-documentation links fall back to the native reference index only when no generated individual page exists; they are flagged as such. A related synthetic graphic is not necessarily a fit from the exact named orchestration route, especially sparse multilevel and partial-path prediction. Plots are rendered in R before publishing, not recomputed in browser JavaScript.

Evidence and boundaries

The website overlay checks source NAMESPACE exports, the 81-plot native R catalogue, generated figure PNGs and reproducible scripts, versioned workflow definitions and internal navigation links. A headless Chromium browser suite checks desktop/mobile behavior, CSV privacy, malformed records, local file input, summary downloads, filtering, selection refusals and figure navigation. The portal page also sets a restrictive content security policy forbidding network connections. Passing website tests is not evidence of numerical parity, estimator calibration, correct missingness identification or external scientific validation.

The frozen R 0.4.3 independent scientific source review plan records 0/508 independently FULL-domain certified Python source contracts. The corresponding Python 1.2 workflows are documented separately. See R Validation, the live Plotting Atlas, generated route JSON and build manifest.

No changes are made to the frozen R 0.4.3 package, Python 1.2 wheel, Zenodo archive, or CRAN submission status.
